W1_ledger_lives_in_a_rebindable_closure_.why: entries is a nonlocal binding mutated by _seal; Python exposes it as a cell reachable via loader.__closure__, and CPython 3.11.3 permits cell.cell_contents assignment
W1_ledger_lives_in_a_rebindable_closure_.module_comment_is_true_of_object_false_o: construction is the only mutation point: _seal rebinds the tuple; no caller can mutate a retrieved ledger object in place - the retrieved OBJECT cannot, the CELL can

W2_authenticated_state_is_caller_constru.why: _AuthenticatedResolverState is a module-level NamedTuple, so any caller may construct one; the guard `if state.owner_ref() is not resolver` reads the FIRST FIELD OF THE STATE ITSELF, so it is a self-declared field the forger sets, not evidence of custody

W3_custody_hash_is_a_transcription_not_a.consequence: a forged state carrying the SOURCE's custody_hash while bound to the VICTIM is undetectable; the genuine custody content is self-consistent so _validate_positive_from_owner_state runs clean

invariants_that_would_defeat_cell_rebind: Non-forgeable custody binding: derive the owner binding from something the caller cannot set (e.g. a secret per-instance token written by the constructor and compared by the guard), rather than a self-declared owner_ref field.
Re-derive custody_hash at decision time from the owning resolver and compare against the state's recorded hash.
Remove _AuthenticatedResolverState from the caller-constructible surface so a forged state cannot be built even given a rebindable cell.
Make the ledger owner-addressed and immutable at import time rather than a mutable cell binding.
note_on_invariant_2_alone: insufficient on its own if the forger can recompute the hash, which they can since semantic_hash is public and the source custody material is available. The durable fix is invariant 1 or 3.
